text: dsh-opencode-usage 是面向 DSH Web 的 OpenCode 用量插件，在 composer 输入栏加入环形用量按钮，点击后打开面板查看 Zen 余额及 Go 的滚动 5 小时、每周和每月用量窗口。宿主端注册同源 JSON 路由读取并缓存 OpenCode 页面数据；面板支持手动刷新和编辑 cookie、workspace ID 等配置。适合希望在 DSH 中快速查看 OpenCode 额度的用户。需要 OpenCode workspace ID 和登录 cookie；数据请求发送至 opencode.ai。

dsh-opencode-usage adds a button to the DSH web composer for viewing OpenCode Zen balance and rolling 5-hour, weekly, and monthly Go usage. Its panel supports refresh and configuration edits. It requires an OpenCode workspace ID and login cookie; requests go to opencode.ai.
想在 DSH 里直接查看 OpenCode 的余额和额度。
OpenCode Go 的 5 小时、每周和每月用量在哪里看？
Can I check my OpenCode Zen balance and Go usage without leaving DSH?
dsh-opencode-usage 的功能「composer 用量面板」：在 DSH Web 输入栏显示环形按钮，点击后打开面板查看 Zen 余额和 Go 的 5 小时、每周、每月用量窗口。
dsh-opencode-usage 的功能「刷新与配置」：在用量面板中手动刷新数据，并编辑 OpenCode cookie、workspace ID 和 peak-clock 显示设置；保存配置后会使缓存失效。
dsh-opencode-usage 使用 OpenCode 登录 cookie 和 workspace ID 请求 opencode.ai 的 Zen 与 Go 页面以读取用量；这两项配置须由用户提供。
dsh-opencode-usage 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 86 天；提交数 2；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。

dsh-opencode-usage README · dsh-opencode-usage：A [dsh](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh) web GUI plugin that shows your
OpenCode Zen balance and Go usage windows right in the composer tool row: a
concentric-ring button (rolling 5h / weekly / monthly) that opens a usage
panel.

dsh-opencode-usage README · dsh-opencode-usage：- **Host half** (`src/index.ts` → `lib/index.js`): resolves config from env
  vars and `$DSH_HOME/ocgo-usage.json`, fetches the opencode.ai SSR pages,
  and serves same-origin JSON endpoints with caching + failure cooldown.
- **Browser half** (`src/client.tsx` → `lib/client.js`): renders the
  concentric-ring composer button and usage panel, and the config editor
  (cookie values are only ever shown masked — the full cookie never leaves
  the host).

dsh-opencode-usage README · Features：- Rolling 5-hour / weekly / monthly usage rings on a single composer button
- Usage panel with window details and a manual refresh
- Built-in config editor in the panel (masked cookie tails only)
- Smart cookie normalization: paste the raw auth token, a full header, or
  anything in between
- Server-side cache (default 5 min) + 60 s failure cooldown so the poller
  never spams opencode.ai
- Optional peak-clock display (`showPeakClock`)

dsh-opencode-usage README · From a local checkout (or a tarball), add into the dsh web profile:：dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-opencode-usage
```

`cordis.patch.yml` inserts the plugin as `opencode-usage`; it requires the
`webServer` service.

dsh-opencode-usage README · Configuration：| Env var | Config file key | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OPENCODE_GO_COOKIE` | `cookie` | — | OpenCode Go session cookie (auto-normalized) |
| `OPENCODE_GO_WORKSPACE_ID` | `workspaceID` | — | OpenCode workspace id |
| `OPENCODE_GO_BASE_URL` | `baseUrl` | `https://opencode.ai` | Provider base URL |
| `OPENCODE_GO_CACHE_TTL` | `cacheTTL` | `300` | Cache TTL in seconds, clamped to `[60, 3600]` |
| `OPENCODE_GO_TIMEOUT_MS` | `timeoutMs` | `15000` | Fetch timeout in ms |
| — | `showPeakClock` | `false` | Show the peak-clock readout |

dsh-opencode-usage README · Configuration：The cookie is **never logged**. You can also edit `cookie` / `workspaceID` /
`showPeakClock` from the panel's config editor; a successful write invalidates
the cache so the next poll uses the fresh values immediately.

Config file is written with `chmod 600`.

dsh-opencode-usage README · API：The browser half talks to the host over plain same-origin JSON:

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/opencode-usage` | Cached usage view |
| `GET` | `/api/opencode-usage/refresh` | Force a fresh provider query |
| `GET` | `/api/opencode-usage/config` | Masked config view |
| `POST` | `/api/opencode-usage/config` | Write cookie / workspace / showPeakClock |

dsh-opencode-usage README · Development：```bash
npm install      # dev deps (esbuild) — prepack build runs automatically
npm run build    # emit lib/client.js + lib/index.js
npm run watch    # hot-swap rebuilds into a running `dsh web` host
```

The build mirrors the dsh plugin loader contract: the browser bundle rides in
the closure-factory module format with react/platform modules externalized,
and CSS is inlined idempotently (`data-plugin-css`).
